job.style: a passage rich in numbers, dates or measurements

passage: In a mature oak tree, growth is not uniform; it is restricted to specific regions called meristems, which allow the tree to increase in height and girth over 50 to 100 years. Unlike animals, plants rely on specialized tissues like xylem and phloem. Xylem, composed of dead cells, provides structural support and transports water and minerals exclusively in an upward direction from roots to leaves. Conversely, phloem transports food synthesized in leaves to all parts of the plant, including roots and growing buds. Within the human body, tissues perform diverse functions. Blood, a fluid connective tissue, contains living cells suspended in plasma, proving that tissues do not need to be solid or fixed to function. Furthermore, the human body contains involuntary muscles, such as those in the heart, which function automatically without conscious effort. Epithelial tissue is also highly versatile; it forms the protective lining of the skin, but it also lines internal organs like the stomach and intestines to facilitate absorption and secretion. These tissues work together, ensuring that even structures like bones, which contain living cells and blood vessels, remain dynamic parts of our biological system. By 2024, biological research continues to confirm that these specialized tissues are essential for the survival of both plants and animals.

items.evidence: In a mature oak tree, growth is not uniform; it is restricted to specific regions called meristems, which allow the tree to increase in height and girth over 50 to 100 years.
items.q: An oak gets taller and wider for decades. Where in the tree does this happen?
options: Only in a few special regions
Evenly in all parts of the tree
Only in the dead xylem cells
Only in cells with large vacuoles
items.explain: Plant growth is not uniform; it happens only in special regions called meristems.

wrong.why: thinks plants grow evenly everywhere like animals
picks a nearby tissue named in the passage
thinks all plant cells are alike and all grow

items.evidence: Xylem, composed of dead cells, provides structural support and transports water and minerals exclusively in an upward direction from roots to leaves.
items.q: Xylem in an oak tree is made of dead cells. What role do these cells play?
options: They support the tree and carry water upward
They are waste with no use to the tree
They carry food from leaves to the roots
They carry water both upward and downward
items.explain: Though dead, xylem cells support the tree and carry water and minerals only upward.

wrong.why: thinks dead plant cells are useless waste
thinks xylem moves water both ways

items.evidence: Conversely, phloem transports food synthesized in leaves to all parts of the plant, including roots and growing buds.
items.q: Food made in leaves is needed by both roots and new buds. How does phloem handle this?
options: It carries food to roots and buds alike
It carries food only down to the roots
It carries food only up toward the buds
It hands the food to xylem to carry
items.explain: Phloem carries food from leaves to all parts of the plant, both roots and growing buds.

wrong.why: thinks phloem only moves food downward
reverses the one-way idea from xylem
mixes up the jobs of xylem and phloem

items.evidence: Blood, a fluid connective tissue, contains living cells suspended in plasma, proving that tissues do not need to be solid or fixed to function.
items.q: Blood flows and is not solid. Why is it still called a tissue?
options: Its living cells work together in plasma
Its cells all touch each other closely
It turns solid once it leaves the body
It flows inside fixed, solid blood vessels
items.explain: Blood has living cells in plasma; tissues need not be solid or fixed to function.

wrong.why: thinks a tissue is just cells touching
still believes a tissue must be fixed in place

items.evidence: Epithelial tissue is also highly versatile; it forms the protective lining of the skin, but it also lines internal organs like the stomach and intestines to facilitate absorption and secretion.
items.q: Why does the inside of the stomach have a lining of epithelial tissue?
options: To help absorb and release substances
To shield it from sunlight, like skin
To let us move it whenever we choose
To join it to bones, like tendons
items.explain: Epithelium is not only on skin; it lines the stomach to help absorption and secretion.

wrong.why: thinks epithelium only does the skin's job
thinks we control all body parts at will
mixes up connecting tissues with linings
